paper.title_en: Design and nonlinear optimization of a one-fold lattice for the Super Tau-Charm Facility collider rings
paper.abstract_en: The Super Tau-Charm Facility (STCF) is a proposed high-luminosity electron-positron collider operating at beam energies of 1–3.5 GeV, with a nominal peak-luminosity target exceeding <math display="inline"><mrow><mn>0.5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>35</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>  </mtext><msup><mrow><mi>cm</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mtext> </mtext><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> at 2 GeV. At such low energies, the combined effects of beam-beam interactions in the crab-waist collision scheme, collective effects, and Touschek scattering impose stringent requirements on the dynamic aperture, momentum acceptance, and beam lifetime. This paper presents the design and nonlinear optimization of a one-fold lattice for the STCF collider rings. The design procedure consists of three main steps: lattice-independent optimization of the global machine parameters under luminosity, beam-beam, collective effects, and lifetime constraints; design of a compact interaction region (IR) with local chromatic correction and dedicated crab-waist sextupoles; and full-ring nonlinear optimization. The last step employs a two-stage strategy combining analysis-driven preoptimization with tracking-based refinement. Particular emphasis is placed on controlling momentum- and amplitude-dependent nonlinearities in the IR and preserving the nonlinear transparency of the crab-waist sextupole pair. At 2 GeV, the optimized lattice achieves a theoretical peak luminosity of <math display="inline"><mrow><mn>1.1</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>35</mn></mrow></msup><mtext>  </mtext><msup><mrow><mi>cm</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mtext> </mtext><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> while maintaining sufficient dynamic aperture, momentum acceptance, and a Touschek lifetime of approximately 600 s. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed staged optimization strategy and provide a systematic framework for the design of high-luminosity, low-energy electron-positron colliders.
